Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
257 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Issued Gale Watches for late Wednesday night through about
midday Friday. Models are tending to lean toward a heavier 
rainfall this Thanksgiving Day with a chance for a few rumbles 
of thunder with an approaching coastal low pressure system from 
the south. Winds will also increase rapidly Wednesday night and 
continue through the day Thanksgiving.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Cooler through mid week.

- 2) A coastal low pressure system will bring the potential for
  heavy rain, damaging winds, and coastal flooding, as well as a 
  little snow and ice in the mountains late Wednesday through 
  Friday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cooler through mid week.

A notable change in the pattern takes place this evening as a 
secondary surge arrives. This ushers in a period of brisk winds 
along with falling temperatures and dew points. The result is a 
return of seasonably cold overnight conditions. Tonight's lows 
will mainly be in the 30s east of the Blue Ridge, with mid/upper
20s off to the west.

The temperature forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday are almost 
mirror images of one another. Daily highs range from the mid 40s
to mid 50s, locally a bit cooler in the mountains. Between the 
two days, Tuesday will provide ample sunshine as a broad surface
high tracks from the Midwest. By Tuesday night, a stout 1042-mb
ridge sits across New England which will make for a cold night 
over the local area. Forecast lows fall into the mid teens to 
mid 20s. For those along and east of I-95, upper 20s to near 
freezing temperatures are more likely. Heading into Wednesday, 
skies will cloud up through the day ahead of the potent 
Thanksgiving Day system. Any impacts largely hold off until 
Wednesday night as northeasterly winds pick up in earnest. 
Although timing varies between models, gusty showers are 
forecast to lift northward across the area overnight. For more 
information on this storm, check out Key Message 2 (below).


KEY MESSAGE 2...A coastal low pressure system will bring the 
potential for heavy rain, damaging winds, and coastal flooding,
as well as a little snow and ice in the mountains late 
Wednesday through Friday.

A coastal low pressure system near the Southeast U.S. Coast 
Wednesday night will become more developed and intensify as it 
moves northward toward the Mid-Atlantic for Thanksgiving Day 
into early Friday. The impacts of the coastal low pressure 
system will depend on the exact track of the coastal low, the 
connection to the upper-level low in support, and timing moving 
up the coast. The general trends in the last few model cycles 
have been slower, stronger, and a bit further west, but still 
with moderate spread.

Light to moderate rain should move into southern parts of our region 
overnight Wednesday into early Thanksgiving as the coastal low is 
over the eastern Carolinas. Increasing northeast to easterly winds
will also occur overnight Wednesday and become quite gusty heading
into Thanksgiving Day. As the winds remain strong to perhaps 
damaging, rainfall could become a prolonged period of moderate 
to heavy rainfall on Thanksgiving. The origin of part of this 
system in the tropical East Pacific into the Caribbean along 
with strong to extreme moisture transport in intense onshore 
low-level winds approaching 80 knots may lead to very efficient
rainfall rates despite limited instability (MUCAPE less than 
250 J/kg). The heaviest rain would most likely occur as the 
coastal low moves out of eastern North Carolina and into 
southeastern Virginia. It would be at this point in time that 
everything is occurring all at once...strong low pressure 
nearby, moderate to heavy rainfall leading to 1 to 3 inches 
total, sustained winds of 15 to 30 mph gusting 35 to 50 mph or 
so, minor to moderate coastal flooding along the western shores 
of the Chesapeake Bay and the tidal Potomac River, and slightly 
above average temperatures.

Much of the rainfall should taper or come to an end from southwest 
to northeast, winds diminishing and becoming more southwesterly as 
the low pressure exits, and temperatures start to fall gradually. 
Coastal flooding may still be a factor as it may take a little more 
time to recede once the low exits.

A little rain and snow mix, or light snow may unfold overnight 
Thursday into Friday over the Alleghenies as the secondary low 
pressure system moves in place of the coastal low and starts to 
push out to the east. It's a little early to see how much snow 
accumulation could occur, but with the unfavorable (south-of-
west) wind direction, upper low support, and colder air, there 
should be some accumulation on the mountaintops.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
While a few showers are possible (mainly near/south of DCA and
east of CHO) through this evening, do not anticipate much in the
way of restrictions. Expect prevailing northwesterlies with 
gusts picking up to around 20 knots through this evening. 

VFR conditions continue into Tuesday and Wednesday as stout high
pressure builds to the north. Winds in turn become northerly 
for Tuesday before shifting to northeasterly Tuesday night into 
Wednesday. Any sub-VFR conditions should hold off until 
Wednesday night as a potent system impacts the region into 
Thanksgiving Day. Overnight northeasterly gusts begin to 
approach 25 to 30 knots ahead of daybreak.

IFR to LIFR conditions seem more probable at the terminals with
the approaching coastal low from the south by Thursday morning.
Both wind and rain combinations could drop ceilings and 
visibility quickly or even more persistently Thursday into 
Thursday evening. VFR conditions should develop moreso later 
Thursday evening through early Friday, as precipitation tapers 
and ends and winds shift and diminish. Winds northeast to east 
20 to 25 knots gusts 30 to 40 knots Thanksgiving Day and into 
the evening. Winds becoming southwest and diminishing 15 to 20 
knots gusts up to 25 knots Thursday night and Friday.

&&

.MARINE...
A stronger north to northwesterly surge moves in this evening 
with gusts increasing to 20 to 30 knots into tonight and the 
first half of Tuesday. The northerly winds remain elevated 
through the remainder of Tuesday before winds turn more 
northeasterly by Wednesday. Additional advisories will likely be
needed through Wednesday. Ahead of the strong system arriving 
for Thanksgiving Day, northeasterlies begin to approach near 
gale levels late Wednesday night.

Gale Watches are in effect late Wednesday night through midday 
Friday. Can't rule out at least a brief period of storm-force
gusts mainly over the middle Chesapeake Bay on Thursday. Small 
Craft Advisory conditions likely into Friday afternoon. Winds 
northeast to east 25 to 35 knots gusts up to 45 knots Thursday.
Winds becoming southeast then southwest 15 to 25 knots gusts up
to 30 knots Thursday night into Friday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Winds gradually pick up in intensity this evening into the 
night. This brings in cooler weather for the week, but also 
lower daytime humidities on Tuesday. A stronger coastal system 
is expected to bring wet and windy conditions to the region 
Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day. There is increasing confidence 
this brings wetting rains to the entire area. Gusty winds 
persist into Friday before high pressure approaches from the 
west by the weekend.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Elevated tides will begin to subside this evening in northwest
flow. However, astronomical tides are very high with the
upcoming full moon on Tuesday. This could result in near minor
flooding along vulnerable shoreline through early evening.

A strong coastal low pressure area will move up the Eastern 
Seaboard Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day. Depending on the 
evolution and track, tide levels may rise once again. Model 
progs still vary widely from abnormally low tides to moderate 
tidal flooding due to uncertainty in exact wind direction/
magnitude, which will depend on the track of the low.
